Findings.Message: Prefer fragment shorthand over React.Fragment. The shorthand `<>` says the same thing with less to read, and a named fragment that carries no props is only the long spelling of it.

The object passed as the value prop to the Context provider (at line 1) changes every render, so every consumer of this context re-renders on every render of this component even when nothing it reads has changed. Wrap it in a useMemo hook so the identity is stable between renders.

This JSX tag names a component that has no declaration in scope, so React receives `undefined` where a component was meant and throws at render rather than at build. Almost always a misspelling or a missing import. Import the component, or fix the spelling to match the binding you meant.
